We check the type of value of "Condition" column
```{r}
str(Data)
```

Condition is a character value. Let's to make that R consider "Condition" as categorical value:

```{r}
Data1 <- Data
Data1$Condition <- factor(Data1$Condition)
str(Data1[,1:3])
```
'data.frame':	196 obs. of  3 variables:
 $ bid      : chr  "INF0052" "INF0100" "INF0100" "INF0100" ...
 $ timepoint: int  0 0 4 9 0 4 9 4 9 0 ...
 $ Condition: Factor w/ 3 levels "Ctrl","PPD","SEB": 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 2 ...

 Then, we should transform the TcellProportion column to TCellFrequency and convert to a factor:
 
 ```{r}
 Data <- Data |> mutate(TcellProportion=Tcells_count/CD45_count) |> mutate (TcellFrequency=TcellProportion*100) |> mutate(TcellFrequency=round(TcellFrequency, 1))
 Data$Condition <- factor(Data$Condition)
 ```
 
 We should activate ggplot2 package:
 ```{r}
 library(ggplot2)
 ```
 
 We are going to draw some few layers first:
 ```{r}
 Plot <- ggplot(Data)
 Plot
 ```
 

 
 ```{r}
Plot <- ggplot(Data) + aes(x=Condition, y=TcellFrequency)
Plot
 ```
 

Next, we load in ggbeeswarm package
 ```{r}
 library(ggbeeswarm)
 ```

This is how looks the beeswarm style boxplot:
```{r}
Plot <- ggplot(Data) + aes(x=Condition, y=TcellFrequency) + geom_boxplot() + geom_beeswarm(size=2.5, cex=2.5)
Plot
```
Now we are going to introduce the sex variable and we have to define symbols and fill:
```{r}
Data |> pull(infant_sex) |> unique()
```

```{r}
shape_sex <- c("Female"=22, "Male"=21)
fill_sex <- c("Female"="white", "Male"="black")
```
And this is our final plot:
```{r}
ggplot(Data) + aes(x=Condition, y=TcellFrequency) + geom_boxplot() + geom_beeswarm(size=2.5, cex=2.5, aes(shape=infant_sex, fill=infant_sex)) + scale_shape_manual(values=shape_sex) + scale_fill_manual(values=fill_sex) + theme(panel.grid.major=element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle=45, hjust=1, size=12), axis.text.y=element_text(size=12))
```

let's change the order of x-axis:

```{r}
Data$Condition <- factor(Data$Condition, levels = c("SEB", "PPD", "Ctrl"))
```
And this is how looks:
```{r}
ggplot(Data) + aes(x=Condition, y=TcellFrequency) + geom_boxplot() + geom_beeswarm(size=2.5, cex=2.5, aes(shape=infant_sex, fill=infant_sex)) + scale_shape_manual(values=shape_sex) + scale_fill_manual(values=fill_sex) + theme(panel.grid.major=element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle=45, hjust=1, size=12), axis.text.y=element_text(size=12))
```

# Problem 2

We need to load in CytoML and ggcyto packages
```{r}
library(CytoML)
library(ggcyto)
```

Assign the location of the files
```{r}
Folder <- file.path("C:/Users/Macarena/CytometryInR/course/05_GatingSets/data")
Folder
```

We want to localize the .wps files
```{r}
FlowJoWsp <- list.files(path=Folder, pattern=".wsp", full=TRUE)
FlowJoWsp
```
 And now, we select the file named as "opened"
```{r}
ThisWorkspace <- FlowJoWsp [stringr::str_detect(FlowJoWsp, "Opened")]
ThisWorkspace
```

Next, we set up the workspace
```{r}
ws <- open_flowjo_xml(ThisWorkspace)
ws
```
And the GatingSet
```{r}
gs <- flowjo_to_gatingset(ws=ws, name=1, path=Folder, additional.keys="GROUPNAME")
gs
```
And we stablish what we want to represent in the plot
```{r}
Plot <- ggcyto(gs[6], subset="Tcells", aes(x="CD8", y="CD4")) + geom_hex(bins=200)
```
And I add some little adjustments: plot title bigger ("size" and face is for indicate the bold style) and in the centre of the plot (hjust) and I remove the grid:

```{r}
Plot + theme_bw() + theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5), panel.grid = element_blank())
```
